key_insight: ACE-Data-0 proposes a human-centric ambient capture system that records how perception, motion, manipulation, sound, and touch unfold together in real homes. The key breakthrough is turning everyday human activity into a richer embodied data engine for training and evaluating embodied AI.
problem_solved: Embodied AI lacks datasets that fully capture the continuous perception-action loop across first-person vision, body motion, object interactions, and multi-sensory feedback. Existing datasets are fragmented by viewpoint, modality, or scale, making it hard to model real-world goal-directed behavior.
method: Introduces the Ambient Capture Engine (ACE), a human-centric data collection framework for real home environments.
Captures synchronized multi-modal, multi-scale signals including first-person perception, whole-body motion, dexterous manipulation, object state, sound, and touch.
Organizes data around goal-driven human activities so the evolution of actions and environment states can be studied over time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic foundation for building and evaluating embodied agents that need to understand and act in complex human environments. It can improve training data quality for robotics, multimodal learning, and long-horizon planning.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing home environment capture into a unified embodied dataset

paper_title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Runmao Yao, Yinghao Liu
